sports scholarship = money given to a student because of athletic ability
fair play = playing by the rules and showing respect, even when it costs you
banned substance = a drug or chemical that athletes are not allowed to use
performance-enhancing drug = a drug taken to improve strength, speed, endurance or recovery
drug test = an official check of blood or urine for banned substances
life ban = a punishment that stops someone competing for the rest of their life
hooliganism = organised or spontaneous violence by fans around sports events
racism in sport = unfair treatment or abuse of people because of race in a sporting context
concussion = a brain injury from a blow to the head, common in contact sport
rehabilitation = the process of recovering fitness and skill after injury
VAR = video technology that helps football referees review key decisions
yellow card = a caution from the referee for unsporting behaviour or a foul
red card = a sending-off, leaving the team with one fewer player
sending-off = the act of dismissing a player from the match
gamesmanship = using legal but unsporting tricks to gain an advantage
time-wasting = deliberately slowing the game to protect a lead
diving = pretending to be fouled in order to win a free kick or penalty
transfer fee = the money one club pays another to sign a player under contract
grassroots sport = local, amateur sport that develops participation rather than elite results
elite sport = sport at the highest competitive level, usually professional
